correctness.rationale: The model ODE and coherent-state energy–loss identity are direct consequences of the Lindblad generator. The full complex field has a fixed mixed term \(aA^2/G^2\). With fixed quadratic loss the global energy defect for hyperbolic/sine ramps is \(\int h\prime{}^2+\sigma\int h^2\); the sine branch is positive by the sharp Dirichlet Poincaré gap. In the obstacle regime the exact defect is \(\int_{\mathrm{front}}(h\prime{}^2-k^2h^2)+\int_{\mathrm{tail}}h\prime{}^2+k^2\int_{\mathrm{tail}}(1-F^2)\), nonnegative by the sharp Dirichlet–Neumann gap and the amplitude cap. Equality analysis proves uniqueness. Source-derived evolution and 149 actual numerical consistency checks verified all stated formulas; finite tests alone are not used for universal proof.

value.rationale: At fixed measurable final cavity ergotropy and cumulative dissipated energy, the microwave intensity is an independent real control burden. The result gives its global exact Pareto frontier and unique optimal envelopes over a physically natural monotone class, identifies two sharp phase boundaries with a saturation plateau and yields ~17.49% control derivative-cost reduction at an existing benchmark q=3/8. Those facts go beyond routine renormalization, shape-parameter fitting or a small correction and characterize useful pulse constraints in a lossy quantum battery.
